title: Install and setup are tested in a clean container
what: An end-to-end test runs relay's install from a pipe on a clean Linux machine in a container (Alpine, the harshest: busybox sh, musl, no curl/git/python3; plus one glibc distribution such as Debian, the common case), then the global part, then setup of a sample project and doctor, and checks the results. It runs in the full gate where a container engine is present and says plainly when it is skipped; the unit tests keep using temporary folders. macOS stays covered by the owner's machine and the temporary-folder tests.
why: Owner, 26 Oct: "Для тестирования ты можешь использовать изолированные окружения, контейнеры alpine, думаю это будет полезно для ряда тестов". Facts, 26 Oct: Docker Desktop 29.4.0 runs on the owner's Mac (arm64), podman is installed too; `docker run --rm alpine:3.20` starts in under 1 s with the image cached; bare Alpine 3.20 has no curl, git or python3; install.sh cannot run from a pipe today (it needs deps.toml beside it or ~/relay, install.sh:20-26), which such a test would have caught. Belongs with relay-installs-with-one-command-from-its-own-rep. IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen).
where: tests/ an end-to-end test of install.sh, relay install, relay setup and relay doctor
